```{r}

library(bcdata)
library(tidyverse)
library(readr)
library(knitr)
```


```{r}
bcdc_search("values")
```

The code above is proprietary to bcdata and allows me to search for datasets using key
terms such as "demographics" or "public health."

# Data 

Link to data guide: https://www2.gov.bc.ca/assets/gov/data/statistics/people-population-community/socio-economic/bcstatsnewslettermay2026socioeconomicindex.pdf

Select "2" to get Census Subdivision Data. This type of data aggregates regions
into municipalities, not health regions (which are usually smaller).

```{r}
#| include: false

bc_ses_data <- bcdc_get_data("b-c-socioeconomic-index")
```

# Question

RQ1: How does socioeconomic index differ across different municipal regions in 
British Columbia?

# Simulate

```{r}
set.seed(1738)

simulated_ses_data <- tibble(
  City = c("Victoria", "Oak Bay", "Vancouver", "Burnaby"),
  Economics = sample(1:100, size = 4),
  Education = sample(1:100, size = 4),
  Health = sample(1:100, size = 4),
  Community = sample(1:100, size = 4),
  SEI = rowMeans(data.frame(Economics, Education, Health, Community))
)

simulated_ses_data
```
